About

Kathmandu → Doha → wherever the science takes me.

I grew up taking things apart in Kathmandu, first toys, then microscopes, then my own lab notebooks. I graduated as valedictorian of Budhanilkantha School and moved to Education City, Doha, to study Biological Sciences at Carnegie Mellon University in Qatar.

My thesis-length obsession is RNA biology: the layer where the genome makes its most interesting decisions. I split my week between the wet lab, the command line and the writing desk, because a result you can't communicate is a result you don't have.

In the long run I want to build computational tools that change how biology is done, the kind researchers open the way they open a pipette. I'm looking for research opportunities in computational genomics, and I'm always up for a hard problem.

Current research

Splicing is where the genome gets creative.

Younis Lab · CMU-Q Spring 2026 to now

Dissecting the dark matter of splicing

One gene, many messages, alternative splicing is how a single DNA sequence encodes a whole repertoire of proteins. I analyse differential splicing across cell states with four independent algorithms, leafcutter, DEXSeq, MAJIQ and rMATs, four dialects of the same biological story. My current project builds a confidence matrix, an XGBoost model trained on all four tools' outputs that scores every candidate splicing change and surfaces the biologically relevant ones as a single, exhaustive catalogue for the wet lab to chase.

What I do in the lab

  • Consensus calls, run all four splicing algorithms on the same cell-state comparisons and reconcile where they disagree, so a change is only called when the tools line up.
  • Confidence matrix with XGBoost, a gradient-boosted model that learns from the four tools' outputs, junction reads, exon-level counts, PSI estimates, to score how confident we are in every splicing change and rank them for the wet lab to chase.
  • Dry lab → wet lab, the breast-cancer splicing analysis starts as dry lab in Nepal, and every candidate finding gets validated at the bench in Doha. Same story, both sides of the pipette.
  • Lab tooling, Python and R tools for the splicing pipeline: reproducible analysis scripts, figure pipelines and data prep the whole group actually uses.

About the lab Younis Lab · CMU-Q

The lab that turns one gene into many messages.

The Younis Lab studies post-transcriptional gene regulation, how the spliceosome strips introns out of pre-mRNA with surgical precision, and how splicing mistakes push cells toward disease. Its signature line of work: minor introns, a rare class removed by a specialised spliceosome, act as stress-induced molecular switches whose activity is controlled by the unstable catalytic RNA U6atac. Projects mix dry and wet lab, RNA-seq, high-throughput screening and drug discovery, with undergraduates co-authoring the papers.
